Subject: URGENT: Partial regional network blip — immediate traffic fallback steps and runbook

Sam / Elio —

We’re seeing a targeted networking control-plane disruption affecting our EU and APAC clusters that is intermittently dropping connections for a subset of requests routed through those regions. Your traffic to region-specific endpoints may see increased errors or elevated latency. Immediate summary and ask: 

What we’ve done (already):
- Activated cross-region egress routing for customer traffic where available.
- Deployed a temporary model-fallback (quantized smaller variant) in US to preserve throughput.
- Increased retries on the service mesh for legacy fallbacks.

What we need you to do now (minimal, <10 minutes):
1) If possible, set your client to prefer our global endpoint (api.redwood.com/v1/global) rather than region-pinned endpoints. This forces traffic to the active US/secondary routing.
2) If you use IP allowlists, add 34.210.45.0/24 and 18.197.120.0/24 as temporary egress (these are the cross-region egress IPs).
3) Toggle your region override in the SDK: set region=us-fallback for the next 4–6 hours.

Attached is a short checklist with curl/sample SDK changes. We’ll keep this thread updated with ETA and remediation steps.

Attachments: reroute-checklist.pdf (pdf)

We know this is disruptive — I’ll remain on this thread until we’re fully back to normal.

— Jonas Weber

Quick technical update / preliminary RCA: 

- Root cause (prelim): an orchestrator-level control-plane reconciliation bug at our cloud provider caused a small percentage of BGP control updates to drop inside eu-central and apac-southeast zones. This impacted only external-facing egress for some AZs, not storage or data-plane compute.
- Impact: ~6% of requests routed to eu/apac for the 08:45–10:20 UTC window experienced transient connection resets or 502s.
- Mitigation performed: enabled inter-region hop routing (US egress) and deployed quantized fallback models in US to maintain throughput while we rebuild the affected control-plane agents.
- ETA: Control-plane fix applied; we expect monitoring to show stable reconnection within 2–5 hours. We will not roll back cross-region routing until metrics are green for 60 minutes.

Action items for BrightSocial (already requested but repeating):
- Confirm SDK region override to us-fallback for prod traffic during the window.
- Validate long-running requests use the increased retry policy (we pushed a safer default while this is active).

Reference: interim notes and log excerpt uploaded to incident drive: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/INC-20280509
Attachments: interim-postmortem-notes.md

— Marcus Lin
VP Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: formal post-incident notes, remediation plan, and next steps (BrightSocial)

Elio / Sam —

Thanks again for working through this with us and for validating the fallback path. This message is the formal follow-up after the mitigation window closed and the control-plane agents were rebuilt. Summary + next steps below: 

Timeline (brief):
- 2028-05-09 08:45 UTC: error spike begins in EU/APAC egress.
- 2028-05-09 09:12 UTC: Redwood issued customer notice and opened ticket INC-20280509.
- 2028-05-09 09:30–11:00 UTC: cross-region routing + us-fallback model active.
- 2028-05-09 13:00 UTC: provider-applied control-plane fix; we kept routing for monitoring and completed rollback at 18:10 UTC after 60 minutes of stable metrics.

Impact summary:
- Affected request percent: ~6% of requests routed to EU/APAC during the window.
- Error class: transient connection resets (502/504) affecting long-running token-generation calls.

Remediation & recommendations for BrightSocial:
- Adopt the global endpoint with region override as a standard fallback in your deployment manifests. We’ve included an example snippet in the attached runbook.
- Add a health-check on long-lived requests and retry at the client layer with idempotent semantics.

Compensation:
- We’re issuing a usage credit covering the impacted window, net of retries that completed successfully. Lauren will send the formal credit note and the spreadsheet with timestamps. Expected credit: a one-time prorated credit that appears on your next invoice.

Postmortem & actions (owners):
- Redwood public postmortem (internal/compliance copy): https://drive.redwood.com/incident/INC-20280509
- Action: Harden cross-region BGP reconciliation checks — owner: Marcus Lin — target: 2028-06-02
- Action: SDK defaults: expose a one-line region-fallback toggle in the next minor release — owner: Developer Platform — target: 2028-05-25
- Action: Customer runbook examples + templated IaC snippets for proxies — owner: Jonas Weber — target: 2028-05-18

I’ll set a 45-minute postmortem review for 2028-05-13 10:00 PT; Lauren will share calendar invite and meeting notes. Please reply if you’d like additional folks included.
